_comment: Video-ID zu Klarstellung. Quelle: der angepinnte YouTube-Kommentar aus packages/<slug>.md im Produktions-Repo. Der Build zeigt ihn auf der Videoseite und sammelt alle auf /corrections/. Pflege: beim Packaging eines neuen Videos eine Zeile ergaenzen.
FTGhQcpG_RA: No, there is no gap — that is the part almost every version of this video gets wrong. The electron clouds DO overlap. The overlap is exactly what creates the push, and pushed further it is what a chemical bond is.
fI5VJxcCe84: The part I had no room for: this prediction is not universal equipment. People with passivity experiences — the sense that your own movements are being made for you — show no attenuation at all. In Blakemore et al. 2000 (Psychological Medicine 30:1131-1139) self-produced and externally produced touch rated the same for them. They can tickle themselves.
cbUPlcHJSFs: Two cords or one? Post your count — and add where your family is from, because this number moves by population more than almost anything else in anatomy: about 3 % in parts of East Africa, over 40 % in the Arab Middle East. The comments on this one are genuinely more informative than the video.
TEipugAb-GE: Which side was open for you — and did you have to think about it, or did you already know? Roughly one adult in four or five has no clearly measurable cycle at all, so "both feel the same" is a real answer, not a failed test.
mkOl6-Zz3OM: Before anyone says it: no, this is not "bone conduction adds bass, that's why you sound deeper to yourself." That line is in almost every video on this topic and the primary measurements run against it — Reinfeldt et al. found the bone component leading in the 1-2 kHz mid-range, and Porschmann found air conduction dominating below 0.7 kHz. The bass-boost story is the one thing I left out on purpose.
J2uuDDU1j1Y: Before the physics-literate comment arrives — yes, gravity IS detectable over an extended body, through tidal gradients, and the equivalence principle is explicitly a local statement. That is exactly why every line in this video says "no nerve you own" rather than "undetectable, full stop." Here is the number it costs to be precise: across a 1.8 m body standing on Earth the tidal difference works out to roughly 5.5 x 10^-6 m/s2 — about 0.6 millionths of g, around one part in 1.8 million of your body weight. Real, measurable, and hundreds of thousands of times below anything you can sense.
vWOyopyRX9c: One correction before somebody else makes it, because it is a first-year chemistry fact: it is NOT true that every molecule in you is left-handed. D-amino acids are real and they are in you - D-alanine and D-glutamate in bacterial cell walls, D-amino acids acting as signalling molecules in your brain. The airtight version is the one the video actually says: every *protein* you have ever built was assembled from the left-handed set, because your ribosome will not take the other one. Narrower, and stranger.
AeBnm-AbY6E: The beat there was no room for, and it is the correction a physicist would leave anyway: saying "its clock runs slow" is only half the picture. From where you are standing, yes - the muon's clock is crawling and that is why it survives the trip. But from where the muon is standing nothing about its life is stretched at all. It gets the ordinary 2.2 microseconds. What changes in its frame is the distance: the fifteen kilometres of atmosphere contract to a few hundred metres, and the fall is simply short. Same particle, same arrival, two ways of writing it down, and neither one is more true than the other.
D82fo98Gbdw: The question this video is going to get, so here it is up front: the frogs were fine. Berry and Geim measured the field induced inside the levitating frog at roughly 1.5 gauss - about the strength of a fridge magnet's stray field, nowhere near enough to do anything to a nervous system - and they put it in the paper in as many words: the animals were not electrocuted, and they emerged from their ordeal in the solenoid none the worse. Nothing was being forced. Every water molecule in the animal was simply being pushed, very gently and all at once, and the sum of those pushes happened to equal its weight.
tWgJRVj4fIo: No, you are not still carrying the air from the day you were born. The air in your lungs is swapped with every breath - what has never been empty is the space. And that leftover litre is not dead weight: it holds your air sacs open and keeps gas exchange running in the gap between one breath and the next.
Hx_Ob-85IL4: Yes - center of mass. Same point, two names. They only come apart in a gravitational field that changes across the object, and at human scale on Earth they agree to parts per million, so "center of gravity" is the honest word for it down here.
O9uV2CMhYOo:
Four things 50 seconds could not hold.

1. In wet, living bone most of the voltage from a step is not the collagen. It is a streaming potential: fluid forced through tiny canals past charged walls. Collagen piezoelectricity is real and has been measured since the 1950s - it is the smaller share. That is why the video names both.

2. Does that voltage tell your bones where to get stronger? Maybe. It is a serious hypothesis and still not established. Anyone selling you denser bones through "the piezoelectric effect" is ahead of the evidence.

3. Most push-button lighters use a ceramic called PZT, not protein and usually not quartz. Same effect, a much stronger material.

4. Yes, the twisted strand in the lighter scene looks like DNA. Collagen is a helix too - a triple one, three protein chains wound together.

More videos on the physics your body is quietly doing are on the way.

Which part of your body do you suspect is secretly doing physics?
